title: Bhimsen Joshi's birth chart
metaDescription: Bhimsen Joshi's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.7° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, the Sun holds a opposition to Neptune at 0.1° — close enough to weld identity to imagination. An opposition puts two needs on opposite shores of the same water. Neither drowns; neither gets the whole beach.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 14.7° into Aquarius — the second decan, which the old scheme hands to Mercury. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 1.1° Pisces, Venus holds 13.5° Aquarius, Mars holds 22.5° Scorpio — in the old shorthand, thought steeped in tone and memory; attraction that begins as conversation; effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun to Neptune is the closest call of the day, a opposition within 0.1°. Across the wheel, each body sees the other in full. The old reading is not conflict so much as permanent mutual visibility. Behind it, Uranus trine Pluto at 0.1°, and Saturn square Pluto at 1.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks four placements here. The Sun in Aquarius at 14.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mercury in Pisces at 1.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Scorpio at 22.5° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Libra at 7.3° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 air, 4 water, 1 fire by element and 4 fixed, 3 cardinal, 2 mutable by mode. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.3° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
